variants.headline: Home-world ship reaches the colony
variants.sub: The colony has received the arrival of a home-world ship.
variants.body:
A ship from the home world has arrived in {colony}. The arrival is a concrete event in the colony's connection with its distant origin. Readers considering {target} should distinguish that fact from assumptions about particular goods, passengers or immediate changes in local supply not specified in this report.

For workers, transport matters through the ordinary life it helps make possible. A ship's arrival should therefore be considered with people's needs in view. Labour has no reason to invent a cargo or a price change to make the point that the colony's connections are part of its common undertaking.

We welcome {target} in this assessment. A tangible connection with the home world deserves recognition, while a fair account can acknowledge the arrival without pretending that every need has thereby been satisfied. Ordinary lives should be the measure, not a convenient afterthought.
